title: Harness policy
description: The shape of .harness/policy.json. Two deliberate limits. Unknown top-level keys are tolerated, because the runtime validator is permissive about fields it does not know and a schema that disagreed with it would be a second, silent definition. And two rules are semantic rather than structural, so they are enforced by the config layer instead: 'a severity may only be tightened', and 'a rule id no rule declares is an error' — the schema cannot know which ids exist.

allowedProductPaths.description: The only paths a coder may change. Prefix matching, so 'src/' means 'inside src/'.

protectedPaths.description: Paths that may never change, even when they are inside allowedProductPaths.

maxIterations.description: The upper bound on coder retries.

requiredChecks.description: Package scripts that must exist and must pass as verification gates.

forbiddenCommands.description: Command patterns refused before execution, matched as contiguous token sequences.

allowedAgentCommands.description: Executable names a provider may use. Empty or absent means no restriction.

agentTimeoutMs.description: The bound on one provider invocation. Verification gates keep their own timeout.

maxChangedFiles.description: The most files one coder iteration may change.

onViolation.description: Whether a violation fails the run or is only recorded. Never weakens side-effect control.

rules.description: Disposition per rule id. An id no rule declares is an error, not a silent no-op.

severityActions.description: Overrides of the default severity to action table. Only tightening is accepted; that rule is enforced by the config layer, not expressible here.
